title.narrative: Enhanced energy-efficiency and climate-resilience in neighborhoods and communities in Cuba

description.narrative:
The housing and urban infrastructure, the public space and the urban greenery are particularly vulnerable to environmental effects, extreme weather events and environmental degradation. In Cuba, as in other Small Island Developing States (SIDS), many settlements are located near or at the coast, which makes them highly vulnerable to sea-level rise and extreme weather events, such as cyclones and hurricanes. Housing vulnerability in Cuba is worsened due to a lack of climate-resilient constructive systems and technologies, inadequate building designs, a deficit of construction materials, construction typologies that do not incorporate the dimension of energy efficiency and a current housing deficit. All these factors make communities more susceptible to economic and livelihood losses and partial damage or total loss of critical infrastructure. In addition, the housing sector in Cuba is the main sector that consumes electricity hence emitting significant greenhouse gases (GHG) to the atmosphere and actively contributing to climate change. This context requires actions for developing mitigation and adaptation strategies, for both providing electricity in houses that are not fully electrified and for houses that need to adapt their electricity systems based on renewable energy technologies and adopting energy-saving housing designs and materials which at the same time increase climate resilience and help communities adapt to climate hazards. The objective of the current readiness proposal is to support Cuba in the transition towards climate-resilient and energy efficient housing and neighborhoods in Cuba. The readiness proposal therefore acts as a preparatory phase as part of a long-term strategy to support the Cuban government in the planning and financing of sustainable and climate-resilient housing and urban development projects.
For this, UN-Habitat will collaborate with the three national institutions that are responsible for managing sustainable urban development, neighborhoods and the construction of housing infrastructure: the Ministry of Construction (MICONS), the National Institute of Territorial Planning and Urbanism (INOTU) and the Ministry of Science, Technology and Environment (CITMA) Other offices such as the National Office for the Control of Rational Energy Use (ONURE). As a first step, the proposal will enhance strategic frameworks to address policy gaps, improve sectoral expertise, and enhance enabling environments for GCF programming in low-carbon, climate-resilient investments in the urban infrastructure and housing sector of Cuba. This will be done through: (1) Knowledge generation and sharing regarding climate vulnerability of prioritized settlements and existing gaps in the housing policy for addressing mitigation and climate adaptation, and on adapted financial instruments and best practices and technologies for low-carbon, climate resilient urban and housing development in Cuba; (2) Development of recommendations and prioritization of actions to integrate energy efficiency and climate-resilient considerations into the existing housing policy strategic and regulatory framework; (3) Capacity development of cuban governmental and external stakeholders for improving energy efficiency and climate-resilience in the urban infrastructure and housing sector and for identifying and mobilizing financial resources and reduce risks in low-carbon and climate resilient urban and housing investments in Cuba.
As a second step, building on the knowledge generated and the capacities built trough anterior activities, a draft concept note on sustainable and resilient settlements and housing will be developed. This draft concept note will allow Cuba to access funding from the GCF in order put into practice the recommendations and actions identified through the proposal.
